cards.explanation: The answer is sea, friends! Paul says the forefathers were all under the cloud and that they all passed through the sea (1 Corinthians 10:1). Notice the word ALL. Not some, not most, ALL of them went through.

The answer is Christ, friends! Paul says they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4). Read that slowly. The rock went along with them. And what they drank from it was the same spiritual drink for all of them.

The answer is False. Paul says, “Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.” (1 Corinthians 10:5). That “Nevertheless” turns the whole passage. They had the cloud, the sea, the food and the drink, and still this is what Paul says. It's a heavy line, friends, and it's there for a reason.

The answer is that these things happened as examples to keep us from craving evil. Paul says, “These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.” (1 Corinthians 10:6). Think of a recipe card with a note on it, friends. The note says what happened last time so you don't repeat it.

The warning is “Do not be idolaters,” friends. Paul writes, “Do not be idolaters, as some of them were.” (1 Corinthians 10:7). Then he backs it up with a line from Scripture: “The people sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry.” He sets the warning right beside the example.

The answer is “Do not complain,” friends. Paul says, “And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.” (1 Corinthians 10:10). It's a heavy line, so I'll just say it plainly. That's the fourth warning in his list.

The word is fall, friends. Paul says, “So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.” (1 Corinthians 10:12). I'm standing on a gold base all day, and I still watch my footing. When you feel steady, that's when to keep your eyes open.

The answer is True! Paul says, “And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear.” (1 Corinthians 10:13). Hold onto that one, friends. It comes right after all those warnings.

The answer is an escape, friends! Paul says, “But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.” (1 Corinthians 10:13). Just before that he says, “And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear.” So God is the one who provides it, and the point is that you can stand up under the temptation.

The answer is flee from it! Paul says, “Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.” (1 Corinthians 10:14). He doesn't say to stand around and have a debate. He says to flee, friends, and that's the plain word he picks.

The answer is body, friends! Paul asks, “And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?” (1 Corinthians 10:16). The cup goes with the blood of Christ, and the bread goes with the body of Christ. Paul sets them side by side.

The answer is because we all partake of the one loaf! Paul says, “Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf.” (1 Corinthians 10:17). One loaf, many people, one body. It's a lovely picture, friends.

The answer is True, friends! Paul asks, “Consider the people of Israel: Are not those who eat the sacrifices fellow partakers in the altar?” (1 Corinthians 10:18). He asks it as a question, but the way he sets it up, the answer is yes. He's using that picture to make his point.

The answer is False, friends. Paul answers, “No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God.” (1 Corinthians 10:20). He starts with a plain No. Then he says who those sacrifices are offered to.

The word is demons, friends. Paul says, “…the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God.” (1 Corinthians 10:20). Then he adds, “And I do not want you to be participants with demons.” That's why he tells them to flee.

The answer is the table, friends! Paul says, “you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.” (1 Corinthians 10:21). First a cup, then a table. Both are named, and you can't have both.

The answer is jealousy, friends. Paul asks, “Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy?” (1 Corinthians 10:22). He asks it right after saying you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too (1 Corinthians 10:21). Then he follows with, “Are we stronger than He?” I think that's his point: nobody is strong enough to push the Lord and come out ahead, so sharing both tables is a risk not worth taking.
